name: Saint Scholastica
history: The sister, and by tradition the twin, of Saint Benedict, she consecrated herself to God from childhood and led a community of women near Monte Cassino. All we know of her comes from Saint Gregory the Great, who tells of her last meeting with her brother, when her prayer won a storm that kept him with her through the night. She is patron of Benedictine nuns.
life: Gregory tells that Scholastica and Benedict met once a year at a house near the monastery, since she could not enter it. At their last meeting they spent the day in praise of God and holy conversation. As night fell she begged him to stay and talk until morning about the joys of heaven. Benedict refused, since his rule forbade a monk to spend a night away. Scholastica laid her head on her hands in prayer, and at once a storm broke so violently that he could not leave. ‘What have you done?’ he asked. She answered that she had asked him and he would not listen, so she had asked God, and God had listened. They talked until dawn. Three days later Benedict saw her soul rise to heaven in the form of a dove, and he buried her in the tomb he had prepared for himself. Gregory says she could do more because she loved more.
prayerTo: Saint Scholastica, you loved God and your brother so much that heaven answered your prayer. Pray for brothers and sisters, for families divided by distance or quarrels, and for all Benedictine monks and nuns. Pray for me, that I may love more, pray with confidence and long for the joys of heaven. Amen.
penance: Telephone or write to a brother, sister or old friend you have not spoken to for some time, and pray for them by name tonight.
meditation: She could do more, Gregory said, because she loved more. Where would a little more love change what you are able to do?
